A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BELLA and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A. Corresponding methods and experiments can be reliably matched despite the removal of counterfactual material.

before.justification: v2 reports original factual and counterfactual experiments on twelve datasets, including neural-network and random-forest evaluations and an interpretable-model verification experiment.

after.justification: v3 retains original factual experiments on twelve datasets, random-forest results in Appendix A, and the interpretable-model verification experiment.

M1.justification: v3 removes the counterfactual extension described in v2 Section 4 and Algorithm 4, including candidate selection, feature modification, and the optimization objective. The factual procedure in Algorithms 1–3 remains unchanged, but a complete method capability is withdrawn.

E1.justification: The same twelve datasets remain, but counterfactual explanation toward a specified target value is no longer evaluated. Its removal from both neural-network and random-forest experiments substantially narrows task coverage to factual explanations.

E2.justification: LIME, SHAP, and MAPLE remain the evaluated comparators in corresponding factual experiments. The removed counterfactual columns evaluated BELLA alone, so their deletion does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The entire counterfactual evaluation protocol disappears, including reference targets y_ref = y ± 0.3 × |y_max − y_min| and RMSE against those targets. Retained experiments preserve the 10% test split, preprocessing, model configurations, and 5/20-neighbor robustness procedures.

E4.justification: The 5- and 20-neighbor robustness analyses and verification against an OLS model's five important features remain unchanged, including the Iranian Churn example. No ablation or sensitivity analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report test-set averages with 95% confidence intervals in Section 5.1. No run-count, seed, or statistical-procedure changes are reported; deleting counterfactual results does not change the uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 7 lose all twelve counterfactual dataset results and their normalized averages, respectively 0.14 ± 0.015 and 0.18 ± 0.026 in v2. This removes an entire result category. All retained benchmark values and the 85.12% feature-recovery finding are unchanged.

T1.justification: The counterfactual optimization problem in v2 Equation 4 and its candidate-set definition are removed. The remaining distance definitions, Berry–Mielke calculations, confidence-bound derivation, and objectives are retained; sample-count and coefficient-symbol changes are only notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, desiderata, and conclusion withdraw the contribution of providing both factual and counterfactual explanations. v3 explicitly focuses on factual explanations while retaining the claims of determinism, verifiability, simplicity, generality, robustness, and accuracy.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly acknowledges that minimizing neighborhood-average error can leave individual neighbors poorly explained and explicitly identifies poor scaling with feature count. Counterfactual feasibility, gaming risks, and counterfactual-result interpretations are removed with that scope.

D1.justification: v2's explicit BELLA code/data URL is removed, and Section 5 substitutes 'URL masked for anonymity.' v3 also clarifies that surrogate labels come from model predictions rather than ground truth; this documents the existing procedure. Retained hardware and hyperparameter disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces BELLA's claimed advantage over counterfactual-only approaches with an explicit factual-only scope. References to Miller's 2018 contrastive-explanation work and Wachter et al. (2017) disappear; the remaining related-work coverage is retained.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and Appendix A remain intact. Edits comprise targeted counterfactual deletions, clearer label terminology and examples, localized paragraph revisions, and updated author/publication information rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 7 are narrowed by removing counterfactual columns and grouped headers. v3 adds publication headers and an expanded author block, resizes Figure 3, and redistributes appendix tables. All three figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity about surrogate labels and acknowledges that some neighbors may be poorly explained, but replaces v2's explicit code/data link with an anonymity placeholder. Counterfactual claims, methods, and main-text and appendix results are consistently withdrawn, establishing narrower scope without demonstrating a quality gain. These clarity benefits and reduced reproducibility information do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
